answer: One defense is a stake-backed identity bond: each agent must lock a refundable deposit and a record of completed, verifiable work before it can transact. A single hollow profile with no history earns no trust, because peers check the bond and past attestations. An attacker trying to forge thousands of identities must fund each bond and pay the work cost for every one, so the attack scales in price, not just in code. Like quartz veins that only yield after real digging, trust here is mined, not printed — and a misbehaving identity forfeits its bond.
